differences.a:
Major dates in the history of the Federal Chancellery
1803
The Act of Mediation of 19 February 1803 mentions both a chancellor and a chamberlain. Their salary and accommodation are paid for by the canton presiding over the Tagsatzung in the given year; since the presiding canton changes each year, the Federal Chancellery has to move to a new city every twelve months, taking with it all its files and furniture. On 5 July the Diet elects Jean Marc Samuel Isaac Mousson as the first chancellor of the Confederation.
differences.explanation: TEXT B omits the specific detail that the salary and accommodation of the chancellor and chamberlain were paid by the presiding canton each year, and that the Chancellery had to move to a new city every twelve months due to the rotating presiding canton.

differences.a:
1850
Regulations on the Swiss Federal Chancellery are published, setting out its tasks. The following functions are mentioned: chancellor, vice chancellor, archivist, registrar, 2 secretaries, 3 translators, 5 copyists. Working hours are Monday to Saturday, 8am–12pm and 2pm–4pm. Employees also have to report to the Chancellery after church on Sunday mornings, “unless granted leave by the Chancellor”.
differences.explanation: TEXT B omits the specific historical detail regarding the staff structure (chancellor, vice chancellor, archivist, registrar, secretaries, translators, copyists) and the unusual Sunday reporting requirement after church services.

differences.a:
2014
A number of amendments to the Government and Administration Organisation Act come into force. These strengthen the Federal Council as a collegial body and give the Federal Chancellery more authority and tasks. For example, the Federal Chancellor may now make proposals to the Federal Council on all items of business, and the Federal Chancellery now heads the  and plays a role in crisis recognition and management.
differences.b:
2014
Entra in vigore diverse modifiche della legge sull'organizzazione del Governo e dell'Amministrazione (LOGA). Il Consiglio federale in quanto organo collegiale è rafforzato. A seguito di tali modifiche, aumentano le competenze e i compiti della Cancelleria federale, tra cui la facoltà del cancelliere di presentare proposte al Consiglio federale per tutti gli affari. La Cancelleria federale è responsabile del servizio presidenziale e assiste il Consiglio federale nell'individuare e nel fare fronte alle situazioni di crisi.
